method: 現在Wikipediaがnullの指定8件について、現行draft/evidenceのSHAとknownByを固定WEB witnessへ照合し、候補Wikipedia記事本文の該当導入・節・項目を実読。リンク同一性、関連のみの区別、同名別人、記事側の意味上の留保、初出ゲートの適合を記録。原稿は変更していない。
articleReadTimeNote: ブラウザー取得からこの記録保存までの正確な個別秒時刻は取得されないため、記事の個別readAtUTCは捏造せず、記録作成時刻のみ保存。

fixedWEB.text: As he was worshiping in the house of Nisroch his god, Adrammelech and Sharezer struck him with the sword; and they escaped into the land of Ararat. Esar Haddon his son reigned in his place.

currentReaderIdentity.identityNoteJa: アドラムメレクとシャレゼルはこの節に並んで名を挙げられるセンナケリブの子です。

wikipediaIndependentCheck.identityJa: This is the human son of Sennacherib named Adrammelech in 2 Kings 19:37. The article explicitly gives “known in Hebrew writings as Adrammelech,” identifies him as Sennacherib’s son, and ties the Biblical naming to 2 Kings 19:37. Do not link the same-title deity page; it explicitly says that deity is unrelated to the human.

fixedWEB.text: He sent Eliakim, who was over the household, Shebna the scribe, and the elders of the priests, covered with sackcloth, to Isaiah the prophet the son of Amoz.

currentReaderIdentity.identityNoteJa: 19:2でイザヤの父として名が記されています。

wikipediaIndependentCheck.identityJa: The article identifies Amoz as Isaiah’s father and explicitly lists 2 Kings 19:2, 19:20, and 20:1. It distinguishes Amoz from Amos the prophet. The profile’s first use at 2KI19:2 matches.

fixedWEB.text: The king defiled the high places that were before Jerusalem, which were on the right hand of the mountain of corruption, which Solomon the king of Israel had built for Ashtoreth the abomination of the Sidonians, and for Chemosh the abomination of Moab, and for Milcom the abomination of the children of Ammon.

currentReaderIdentity.identityNoteJa: 神名としての言及で、人物としての経歴は示されません。

wikipediaIndependentCheck.locator: Redirect notice lines 221–223; Israel and Judah section lines 730–737; Philistia section lines 745–751
wikipediaIndependentCheck.identityJa: The Ashtoreth URL redirects to Astarte. The page discusses ʿAštart, its plural biblical form ʿAštārōṯ, and related Israelite/Judahite worship, and separately notes “Ashteroth” in the Philistine narrative. It is relevant to the Sidonian goddess named in 2KI23:13, but it does not establish a simple one-to-one identity for that exact Biblical form; keep the relationship note qualified.

fixedWEB.text: Manasseh was twelve years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Hephzibah.

currentReaderIdentity.identityNoteJa: 21:1にマナセの母として名が挙げられるヘフツィ・バです。

wikipediaIndependentCheck.locator: Introduction and Biblical and rabbinic accounts lines 116–121
wikipediaIndependentCheck.identityJa: The article calls Hephzibah a minor figure in Kings, wife of Hezekiah and mother of Manasseh, and directly cites 2 Kings 21:1. It is the same woman named as Manasseh’s mother at 2KI21:1.

fixedWEB.text: But Jehosheba, the daughter of King Joram, sister of Ahaziah, took Joash the son of Ahaziah, and stole him away from among the king’s sons who were slain, even him and his nurse, and put them in the bedroom; and they hid him from Athaliah, so that he was not slain.

currentReaderIdentity.subtitleJa: アハズヤの子でユダの王
currentReaderIdentity.identityNoteJa: ユダ王アハズヤの子ヨアシュです。イスラエル王ヨアシュとは別人です。

wikipediaIndependentCheck.locator: Introduction lines 172–175; early life lines 182–183; refs lines 249–251
wikipediaIndependentCheck.identityJa: The article names Jehoash as also known as Joash, identifies him as Ahaziah’s surviving son, and discusses his rescue from Athaliah; references explicitly cite 2 Kings 11:2. This is the Judahite Joash, not the Israelite king with the same name. Because the page covers his full life, any reader note should be limited to what is known at the profile gate 2KI11:2.

fixedWEB.text: So he died according to the LORD’s word which Elijah had spoken. Jehoram began to reign in his place in the second year of Jehoram the son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, because he had no son.

currentReaderIdentity.identityNoteJa: 1:17は、アハズヤの兄弟ヨラムと、ユダ王ヨシャファトの子ヨラムを同じ節で区別しています。

wikipediaIndependentCheck.identityJa: The article identifies Jehoram/Joram as king of the northern Kingdom of Israel and explicitly distinguishes the contemporaneous Jehoram of Judah. That matches the Israelite Joram who succeeds Ahaziah at 2KI1:17; the distinction is important because that verse names both kings.

fixedWEB.text: He defiled Topheth, which is in the valley of the children of Hinnom, that no man might make his son or his daughter to pass through the fire to Molech.

currentReaderIdentity.identityNoteJa: 神名としての言及であり、人物の伝記ではありません。

wikipediaIndependentCheck.locator: Spelling and biblical attestations lines 180–190; 2 Kings passage lines 209–213; interpretation debate lines 246–263
wikipediaIndependentCheck.identityJa: The article explains the Molech/Moloch spelling variant and quotes 2 Kings 23:10 directly. It also records scholarly disagreement over whether the term denotes a deity or a sacrificial rite/title. Link only as a related article and retain that uncertainty instead of asserting a settled deity identity.

fixedWEB.text: Jehoiachin was eighteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned in Jerusalem three months. His mother’s name was Nehushta the daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem.

currentReaderIdentity.identityNoteJa: エホヤキンの母として名前が挙がるネフシュタです。

wikipediaIndependentCheck.articleTitle: List of minor Hebrew Bible figures, L–Z
wikipediaIndependentCheck.identityJa: The dedicated Nehushta entry gives her name, identifies her as the wife of Jehoiakim and daughter of Elnathan, cites 2 Kings 24:8, and says she was Jehoiachin’s mother. The profile’s first-use gate at 2KI24:8 matches the cited verse.
